place_fields.vibe: offbeat monsoon waterfall and dam-spillway setting
place_fields.summary: Kitwad Waterfalls is a man-made monsoon waterfall formed by overflow from Kitwad Small Dam near the Maharashtra–Karnataka border.

planning_attributes.description: A seasonal waterfall created when Kitwad Small Dam overflows its spillway.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Kitwad Small Dam is approximately 30.5 m high; a separate waterfall height is not established by the verified sources.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Kitwad Waterfalls is described as a man-made waterfall created by overflow from Kitwad Small Dam.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From Belagavi, travel toward Kitwad village; the final approach to Kitwad Small Dam is a narrow road, followed by about a 2-minute walk to the waterfall viewpoint.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: No formal entry restriction was identified in the verified sources; access is weather-dependent during the monsoon.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Do not enter the fast-flowing spillway or approach slippery edges. Use daylight, grippy footwear, and extra caution around the dam and waterfall.
planning_attributes.notes: Roadside parking and entry are reported as free; conditions and local access can vary in monsoon.

place_fields.micro_region: Sada village, Belagavi district, Karnataka, Western Ghats
place_fields.vibe: remote forest waterfall and strenuous trek
place_fields.summary: Sādagundi/Sada Waterfall is a major waterfall deep in the Western Ghats near Sada village on the Karnataka–Goa border, reached by a long guided trek.

planning_attributes.description: A tall waterfall in a forested Western Ghats setting, with streams, boulders and dense vegetation along the approach.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The Sada trek area includes Sada Fort, step-wells, temples and natural caves along the route.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Road access reaches Sada village; the final approach is on foot. Karnataka Tourism reports a trek of roughly 8–18 km depending on the starting point and trail, with Belagavi about 60 km away.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Camping is not permitted in the forests around Sada according to Karnataka Tourism; guided trekking is advised.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Crossing streams, boulders and leech-prone trails makes this a medium-to-high complexity trek. Avoid heavy rain, carry water/food, and use an expert/local guide.
planning_attributes.notes: Mobile connectivity may be limited on the trail; nearby Sada Fort and caves can be included in the outing.

place_fields.micro_region: Huland, Belagavi district, Karnataka, Western Ghats
place_fields.vibe: jungle waterfall with a short-to-moderate trek
place_fields.summary: Delta Kalasa Falls is a forested waterfall near Huland, Karnataka, with trekking access and a reported drop of more than 100 feet.

planning_attributes.description: A waterfall in dense forest near Huland, with hiking/trekking access and a pool at the base reported by visitors.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Reported waterfall height is over 100 feet.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The site is associated with Kalasa and is described as a natural waterfall in the Western Ghats.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The verified listing places it at Huland; visitor directions describe reaching Delta Ecohuts beside the Goa–Belagavi road and walking downhill to the falls, with other reports describing a longer trek depending on route.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: No formal entry restriction was identified in the verified sources.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The approach can be slippery, with leeches reported in the forest. Exercise caution on the downhill trail and around the waterfall pool and rocks.
planning_attributes.notes: The surrounding forest and trekking route are the main attraction; facilities at the falls themselves are limited.
